steps.title: Describing a scene, and checking you have been understood
steps.html:
Position first, then detail. English descriptions usually move from the whole to the part: in the foreground, in the background, on the left, at the top, behind him, in the middle distance. Give the position, then the object, then the adjectives.

Adjective order, from lesson 41. Opinion → size → quality → shape → age → colour → origin → material. A large black panther, brightly coloured dresses, a stiff green leaf pattern. Two or three at a time; move the rest behind the noun.

Sense verbs, from lesson 43. Can is normal with the senses: I can see, you can almost hear, I could smell. You look at a picture and watch what happens in it. After look, seem and sound, an adjective; with like, a noun.

Impressions and guesses. A photograph does not answer questions, so mark what you are inferring: they seem to be…, it looks as though…, it must be winter, it might be a market, some sort of rope.

Checking. Three different problems, three different phrases. A word you did not catch: Sorry, did you say ‘cooking’? A word you heard but do not understand: What do you mean by ‘on the water’? Your own understanding of the whole idea: Am I right in thinking that…? And when the other person is lost: You look a bit confused, Do you see what I mean?

Summarising a comparison. They are the same in that both are markets, and different in that mine… This is the sentence that ends the recording, and it is worth learning whole.

steps.title: The commonest errors at this level
steps.html:
• on the foreground — it is in the foreground.
  • What do you mean with…? — the preposition is by.
  • They seem be women — seem to be.
  • It looks stiffly — an adjective after look.
  • a black large panther — size before colour.

steps.title: Напиши свой текст
steps.sub: Напиши ответ, затем сверься с образцом
steps.modelHtml:
The painting is almost square, and at first it reads as a wall of green. Only after a few seconds do you find the two things it is actually about: an animal on the left, and a small figure in the top right corner that most people never see at all.

In the foreground there is a large black panther, standing rather than crouching, with its head turned away from us. It is impossible to tell whether it is about to pounce or has just decided not to. Around it the jungle is too orderly to be real: the same stiff leaf pattern repeats eleven times, and the leaves look as though they had been cut out of metal and painted afterwards. A length of thick brown rope hangs from the branch above the animal, which nobody has ever explained.

In the background the sky is threatening, a heavy grey-green that does not appear anywhere else in the picture. The small figure stands under it in rubber boots, which is the detail that dates the painting, and seems to be carrying something. It might be a lamp; it might be a bird. The border around the whole scene is purely decorative, and it is the only part with any red in it.

What is remarkable is how quiet it is. Every predator in the picture is looking away from the viewer, and there is no wind in the stiff leaves. You would expect to hear a clatter from somewhere and you can hear nothing, which is probably why colour-blind visitors, who see the greens as one flat tone, often describe it as the calmest thing in the room.
